Results: 930 patients were included in the intent-to-treat population
(ropinirole/H11005464; placebo /H11005466). At week 12 LOCF there was a statisti-
cally signiﬁcant treatment beneﬁt in favor of ropinirole, compared with
placebo, for mean change from baseline in IRLS total score (p /H110210.001) and
for proportion of responders on the CGI-I scale (p /H110210.001). The IRLS total
score correlated with CGI-I response (0.71). Of the IRLS subscales, the
symptom subscale had a higher correlation with CGI-I response (0.73) than
the symptom impact subscale (0.45).
Conclusions: Ropinirole treatment effectively improves RLS symptoms,
as measured by the IRLS and proportion of CGI-I responders. Response on
the CGI-I scale and the IRLS total and symptom subscale is highly
correlated and deserves further investigation.
P380
Treatment resistant jerky stiff person syndrome
T. P. Harrower, R. Barker, J. Baron, A. Coles (Cambridge, United
Kingdom)
Background: Stiff Person Syndrome (SPS) is a well recognized autoim-
mune mediated condition with an association with antibodies to glutamic
acid decarboxylase (GAD). Less well deﬁned is the condition of Jerky SPS,
an atypical form of SPS.
Methods: Here we present a case of a 28 male who initially presented
with neck and back pain, and generalised stiffness associated with jerks in
his neck. Over the next few months the jerky muscle activity spread to
involve his shoulder girdle (see video). Clinical examination conﬁrmed the
presence of regular spasms resembling myoclonic jerks in the shoulder
girdle region with generalised stiffness but no other general or neurological
deﬁcits.
Results: Besides the presence of an elevated anti-GAD titre initially 12
rising to 105 (normal range less than 10 ng/ml) tests have been normal
including neuroimaging, somatosensory evoked responses. But electro-
myography demonstrated episodes of spontaneous motor activity. General
investigations (including tumour markers, whole body CT and FDG-PET
scanning) have failed to demonstrate an occult malignancy. Immunomodu-
latory therapy including, steroids, plasma exchange, intravenous immuno-
globulin and rituximab (monoclonal antibody directed against B cells) has
reduced the anti-GAD antibody titre to within normal limits (3.6 ng/ml) but
has failed to produce any clinical beneﬁt beyond a mild response to high
doses of benzodiazepines during 36 months of follow-up.
Conclusions: We therefore demonstrate a case of Jerky SPS reafﬁrming
the presence of an atypical SPS phenotype in the absence of a malignancy
which has failed to clinically respond to immunotherapy despite a sero-
logical response.
P381
Aceruloplasminemia with marked brain iron overload treated for nine
years without neurological deﬁcit
J. D. Gowing (Cambridge, ON, Canada)
Aceruloplasminemia is an auto recessive disorder of iron metabolism
which usually presents with severe neurological problems as a result of
iron overload in the brain. We present a case of a forty two year old
caucasion female who presented in 1997 with a history of glucose intol-
erance and fatigue. There were no abnormal neurological ﬁndings. There
was no family history of iron overload or neurological disorders.
Laboratory ﬁndings included normal Hemoglobin and MCV.
Ferritin was 989ug/L and iron saturation was 0.05% Liver and bone
marrow biopsies revealed gross iron overload. DNA studies for Hereditary
Hemochromatosis were normal.
After many phlebotimies she developed a microcytic anemia. At this

stage a ceruloplasmin level was 0. DNA studies done at Shinshu Univer-
sity, Japan were in keeping with a stop codone in the sequencing of the
exon 4.
Ceruloplasmin rich plasma from four donors was supplied by the Ca-
nadian Blood service and administered on a weekly basis and phlebotimies
were resumed. Over 100 liters of whole blood have been removed. The
patient continues to be free of neurological deﬁcit. MRIs of the brain have
shown little change but MRI estimations of iron content of other organs is
now normal.
The patient developed proliferative glomerulonephritis which is now her
main problem. MRI and laboratory changes over nine years are presented.
P382
The long-term effect of botulinum-toxin for post-whiplash pain
syndrome
C. Braker, S. Yariv, R. Adler, S. Badarny, E. Eisenberg (Haifa, Israel;
Afula, Israel)
Background: Myofascial pain syndrome characterized by local pain and
stiffness, trigger points may evolve after whiplash injury.Some patients
will develop a chronic,pain syndrome. Botulinum neurotoxin type A has
shown controversial results in term of its effectiveness for post whiplash
chronic neck pain.
Objective: The aim of study is to test the long-term efﬁcacy of early-on
trigger point injection of botulinum neurotoxin type A, in relieving Myo-
fascial neck pain in patients with post-whiplash injury.
Methods: 20 patients with cervical Myofascial pain, 2-48 weeks after
whiplash injury, were randomly assigned to receive either 200U of Botox
or placebo group into 4 trigger points (10 patients/group). Eighteen patients
(9in each group) completed a six-month follow-up. Outcome measures
included intensity of pain evaluated by a 0-10 VAS Scale, 0-4 Numerical
Pain Scale (NPS) of maximal and average pain intensities during the
preceding week, and “pain diaries” using VAS 0-10. Quality of life
evaluated by the SF-36 questionnaire and global assessment of the treat-
ment efﬁcacy completed by the physician and the patients, the intensity of
unpleasantness and pain in response to pressure algometer, range of cer-
vical motion, adverse effects and consumption of other therapies. All
parameters were recorded in each visit (baseline and 3, 6, 9, 12 and 24
weeks after the injections).
Results: A time dependant improvement in all tested parameters was
found in both groups. All parameters showed a consistently larger improve-
ment in the botulinum treated group compared in the placebo, but not at a
signiﬁcant level.
Conclusions: The results are consistent with those of earlier small trials,
indicating a greater effect in the treatment group without statistical signif-
icance. It is difﬁcult to determine whether the lack of signiﬁcant effect is
a result of the small sample size and several other limitations of the studies
or from lack of therapeutic effect,the use of botulinum neurotoxin remains
an optional therapy for selected patients.
P383
Reversible multifocal neuro-radiological syndrome in acute on chronic
porto-systemic encephalopathy
A. Aggarwal, A. Nagral, S. Shah, K. Ganesan, M. Bhatt (Mumbai, India)
We report 2 patients with reversible multifocal neurologic signs on
background of acute on chronic porto-systemic encephalopathy (PSE).
Patient 1: 24 year man had non-cirrhotic portal ﬁbrosis for 2 years. During
esophageal variceal embolization he became comatose and required ven-
tilatory assistance (Grade IV PSE). There was persistent asymmetric spas-
tic quadriparesis (MRC grade 2/5 right; 0/5 left). CT showed diffuse

cerebral edema without brainstem compression. Electroencephalogram
showed diffuse slowing and bi-frontal triphasic potentials. With antihepatic
coma treatment he regained consciousness in 1 week, could walk with
support in 2 weeks and independently in 8 weeks. Mild left spastic
hemiparesis (MRC grade 4/H11001/5) persists, 18 months later. Patient 2: 42 year
man had cryptogenic cirrhosis (Child Pugh C) with portal hypertension for
3 years. Over 3 weeks he developed scanning dysarthria, bilateral inten-
tional tremor, severe truncal and gait ataxia and left spastic hemiparesis
(MRC grade 4/5) with grade 1 PSE. Ataxia was disabling. With antihepatic
coma treatment, in 4 weeks, he walked independently. In both patients, at
maximal deﬁcit arterial ammonia was elevated and MRI showed wide-
spread bilateral cortical, perisulcal white matter and cerebellar T2W hy-
perintensities which were hypo/isointense on T1W images with areas of
hemorrhages. Serial MRI (over 18 months in patient 1; 6 months in patient
2) showed remarkable albeit incomplete resolution of these changes in
parallel with clinical recovery. Both had pallidal manganese deposits on
MRI, suggesting chronic PSE.
